title: Launch Runway Synapse: Coordinated Cutover & Dependency Orchestration for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: create a runnable launch runway and orchestration playbook that coordinates cutover windows, dependency handoffs, and capacity lanes across Runtime, Console, and API teams. This ticket delivers the end-to-end plan, owner roster, preflight telemetry checks, rollback triggers, and a lightweight automation spec for enforcing blackout windows and capacity reservations.

Scope: 1) Establish a canonical launch calendar with per-region windows and throttling lanes; 2) Define dependency ownership and strict handoff SLAs between runtime, console, and API services; 3) Create a preflight checklist (telemetry health, smoke tests, canary traffic percentages, fallback model mapping) that each team must sign off before cutover; 4) Design an escalation and rollback decision tree with clear metrics for automatic rollback; 5) Produce a minimal automation spec (GitHub Actions & PagerDuty runbook hooks) to gate merges and deployments during launch windows.

Why now: multiple 2026-Q2 launches (runtime-2.0 model routing, console rollout for per-route dashboards, API structured-output contract) are overlapping. Without a single source of truth for windows and capacity lanes we risk cross-service contention, surprise rate limits, and last-minute rollbacks. This effort reduces blast radius and improves predictability for customers and sales/CS handoffs.

Stakeholders: Product (release managers), Runtime Eng, Console Eng, API Eng, SRE, Observability, Solutions Engineering, Legal (for customer notices).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical launch calendar published and accessible from Console (read-only view) with per-region windows and TTL for updates
Owner roster and day-of contacts defined for each service and region; on-call rotations assigned for launch days

Preflight checklist documented with at least 6 telemetry checks (latency p95, error budget remaining, queue depth, token-cost delta, model fallbacks healthy, rollout traffic success) and pass/fail thresholds
Automated gating spec implemented in GitHub Actions that prevents merges into release branches during blackout windows unless override approved via Slack + approver list
Rollback decision tree validated in a tabletop run and documented with explicit metrics that trigger rollback (e.g., sustained >3x error rate, p99 latency regression >200ms, customer-impact >= high)
Capacity reservation lanes defined and communicated: baseline, burst, and emergency lanes with quotas and cost owner
Post-launch runbook template created for collecting incident timelines, customer notices, and L2/L3 postmortem data
